$comment: Soft contrast (§5.20) — high contrast with the glare taken off.
Dan's ask, 2026-07-31: 'high contrast, but the white text is just a little
bright'. So this is the same idea — structure from edges, not from surface
tints — with pure white and pure black pulled back one step: text is a warm
off-white and the surfaces are near-black with a slight blue cast rather
than #000. Status hues are the high-contrast ones, desaturated a touch.
It is a COMFORT theme that still clears the accessibility bars: every pair
in tokens.drift.test.ts is asserted at the same thresholds as high contrast
(body text >= 7:1 AAA, secondary >= 4.5:1, structural edges >= 3:1). Body
text lands at 12.7:1 where high contrast is 21:1 — softer by design, not by
accident, and the test is what keeps that true.
The lifts are real here rather than transparent: this theme is allowed a
little depth, which is most of what makes it feel gentler.
It is a SECOND data file and it needed no code change — one line in
builtin-themes.ts and one string in en.json. That is the whole point of
P2-E15-05, demonstrated by the first theme that was not in the plan.
